conviction_note: First standalone print of crop-protection-only Corteva (seed spun into Vylor 2026-10-01); every Q3 crop-protection peer that has reported since Corteva last spoke (FMC, Syngenta, Bayer, ADAMA, UPL) printed weak Latin American volumes and quarter-end destocking while the CP consensus still assumes +4% y/y sales, so the findings lean negative (impact_sum -1.9); p_up is only 44 because the stock is already -10.75% over 20 days (fell 4% on FMC's warning), trades near 6x 2026 EBITDA against sell-side targets of $15-20, and the new company has no reaction history of its own, giving a scaled -0.84 that is smaller than the sum.
bar: Crop-protection-only (continuing perimeter) Q3 2026: revenue ~$1.77bn and EPS $0.09 (Earnings Whispers preview, 2026-11-03, https://www.earningswhispers.com/article/CTVA/22826), i.e. +4% on Q3 2025 CP net sales of $1,701m (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1755672/000175567225000020/a3q_2025xearningsxnewsxr.htm). Consolidated (seed still inside the Q3 books, spin was after quarter end) bar ~$2.65bn / -$0.39 per Benzinga (https://www.benzinga.com/quote/CTVA/earnings-forecasts), which reconciles to CP $1.77bn plus Vylor's own Q3 consensus $883m / -$0.44 (https://therighttrader.com/earnings-calendar/vylr). Company guide: H2 2026 CP volume up high-single-digit, price down low-to-mid single digit (Brazil mid-to-high single digit), Q3 consolidated operating EBITDA a loss of ~$100m or more; investor day 2026-09-15 set standalone New Corteva 2026 at ~$7.8bn sales / ~$1.3bn operating EBITDA (https://quartr.com/events/corteva-inc-ctva-investor-day-2026_3Y0NpwEb). Two bases exist and headlines may compare the consolidated loss with the CP-only $0.09; the bar is reconcilable but not cleanly single-sourced, so sizes kept moderate.
positioning_check: Short interest 21.63m shares, 4.8 days to cover as of 2026-09-30 settlement (pre-spin volumes; https://massive.com/quote/ctva); ~3% of the ~680m shares, and against the post-spin 20-day average volume of 19.6m shares (baseline) about 1.1 days: not crowded, no squeeze mechanism. Earlier: 17.7m / 4.1 DTC in August (https://equibles.com/stocks/ctva/short-interest). Skew: skew_25d_vol_points is null in the baseline (new post-spin chain, ATM spread 16% of mid, total OI 7,444); put/call OI 0.62; ATM IV 72.6% against 33.7% 20d realised, event-implied move 9.53%. So the option market is paying for a large move without stating a direction. Run-up -10.75% over 20d, -2.45% over 5d, 17% below the 52-week high.

findings.finding: FMC's Q3 2026 release (2026-10-29) reports like-for-like revenue -22% and volume -21% because 'channel customers in several key markets sharply reduc[ed] replenishment orders during the final weeks of the quarter' to run very low inventory against high financing costs (Brazil, Argentina, US, Canada), after its 2026-10-15 pre-announcement; Corteva last updated its CP outlook on 2026-09-15 (2026 standalone EBITDA ~$1.3bn, H2 CP volume +HSD) and the CP consensus still sits at ~$1.77bn, +4% y/y.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No standalone CP history: the baseline's eight reactions (median 2.42%) are the combined seed+CP company. The combined company fell 11.9% after the 2026-07-30 print when Q2 sales missed and H2 CP pricing was cut (https://www.agnavigator.com/Article/2026/08/03/corteva-lifts-outlook-but-investors-want-more-than-margin-growth-ahead-of-split/), i.e. it has punished CP top-line disappointments. FMC itself fell ~35% on the 2026-10-15 warning.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: CTVA fell >4% intraday on FMC's warning day (https://stocktwits.com/news-articles/markets/equity/fmc-stock-crashes-on-massive-earnings-downgrade-citi-expects-modest-negative-reaction-for-peer-corteva/cZxhGzwRBr3, 2026-10-15) and is -10.75% over 20 days. Not fully priced because the preview consensus (2026-11-03) still carries CP sales up ~4% y/y in line with the company's +HSD volume guide; if the market had marked Corteva for the same quarter-end destocking, the CP revenue bar would sit at or below last year's $1,701m. Citi argued Corteva's generic exposure is smaller than FMC's, which is why this is sized at a fraction of FMC's own damage.
findings.independence: Same direction from different companies: ADAMA Q3 Latin America -8% with Brazil under pressure (https://www.prnewswire.com/il/news-releases/adama-reports-third-quarter--first-nine-months-2026-results-302923838.html), UPL Q2 FY27 Latin America -8% (https://www.agribusinessglobal.com/agrochemicals/upl-q2-and-h1-fy27-results-upl-sustains-profitable-growth-amid-global-headwinds-and-cost-inflation/), filed separately as the next finding. FMC's 10-15 pre-announcement and the 10-29 release are one fact and counted once here.

findings.finding: Four other crop-protection peers reporting Q3 2026 after Corteva last spoke printed Latin American / crop-protection declines: Syngenta Q3 group sales -10% (-12% cc) with delayed purchases and 9M LatAm CP -14%, Brazil -6% on off-patent pricing pressure (2026-10-30); Bayer Crop Science Q3 -2.4% with core crop protection -6% and fungicides and herbicides ex-glyphosate each -8.6% (2026-11-05); ADAMA Q3 sales -4% (volume -4%, price -2%), Latin America -8% to $286m with Brazil pressured in fungicides and insecticides; UPL Q2 FY27 Latin America -8%, CP volumes -10% to -16% — against a Corteva CP consensus of +4%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Combined Corteva fell 11.9% on the 2026-07-30 print driven by a sales miss and lower H2 CP pricing; no standalone CP reaction exists yet.
findings.why_not_priced: The consensus quoted in the 2026-11-03 preview still embeds CP growth in line with the company's +HSD volume guide; a bar that had absorbed five weak peer quarters would show flat-to-down CP sales. Partly priced through the 20-day -10.75% drift. Corteva has outgrown peers on new products (~$2bn, volume +HSD, flat price per the Q2 call), which is why this is not sized larger.
findings.independence: Separate documents: Bayer https://www.agnavigator.com/Article/2026/11/05/bayers-crop-science-hit-by-weather-and-regulatory-pressures-despite-latin-america/ (2026-11-05); ADAMA https://www.prnewswire.com/il/news-releases/adama-reports-third-quarter--first-nine-months-2026-results-302923838.html ; UPL https://www.agribusinessglobal.com/agrochemicals/upl-q2-and-h1-fy27-results-upl-sustains-profitable-growth-amid-global-headwinds-and-cost-inflation/ ; Syngenta 9M Brazil detail https://www.agribusinessglobal.com/es/agrochemicals/syngenta-group-reports-9m-2026-results-with-higher-profitability/ . Same hypothesis as the FMC finding (peer read-through to Corteva CP), from independent companies; the two together are sized at about 2 points rather than double counted.

findings.finding: The forward guide is the larger line and the peer Q4 commentary is mixed-to-negative for Corteva's standalone 2026 EBITDA of ~$1.3bn (set 2026-09-15): FMC guides Q4 with a high-single-digit price decline and its own Brazil price cuts on channel-held product, UPL flags a possible 'super El Niño' Nov-Mar as a Brazil/LatAm concern, while Syngenta and UPL say some volume was phased into Q4/H2 (the offset).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Combined Corteva sold off on the 2026-07-30 H2 CP pricing cut despite a raised EPS guide; the 2025-10-01 separation announcement day was -9.11%. New Corteva has issued no standalone guide revision yet.
findings.why_not_priced: Nothing in the wire carries a post-FMC estimate of New Corteva's Q4 or 2027; the only standalone numbers are the 2026-09-15 investor-day targets, which predate every peer print. If the market had already marked the $1.3bn down, sell-side targets would not still be $15-20 (UBS $15, GS $20, JPM $19). The Q4 delays into Brazil's main season cut the other way, hence the wide band.
findings.independence: UPL outlook https://www.agribusinessglobal.com/agrochemicals/upl-q2-and-h1-fy27-results-upl-sustains-profitable-growth-amid-global-headwinds-and-cost-inflation/ ; Syngenta delays https://www.agnavigator.com/Article/2026/10/30/syngenta-sales-and-profit-fall-in-q3-as-european-heatwaves-curb-crop-protection-demand/ . Shares the FMC document with the first finding but uses its Q4 line, not its Q3 numbers.

findings.finding: Corteva and EIDP filed an NT 10-Q on 2026-11-10 (separation-related reporting processes), stating Q3 2026 results will show 'a higher seasonal loss as compared to the same period in 2025' because of separation costs and ongoing R&D investment, and that results would be issued before the 2026-11-12 call; Vylor also cannot file on time.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior late filing by Corteva; combined Q3s are seasonal loss quarters (Q3 2025 GAAP loss from continuing operations $308m; operating EPS -$0.23).
findings.why_not_priced: Largely inside guidance: management had already warned of a Q3 operating EBITDA loss of ~$100m or more, so a higher seasonal loss is what the company told the market to expect. Residual: an NT 10-Q is seldom read, and a consolidated loss set beside a CP-only $0.09 consensus can print as a headline miss after hours.
findings.independence: Earnings Whispers preview quoting the guided Q3 EBITDA loss, https://www.earningswhispers.com/article/CTVA/22826 ; no material weakness, restatement or impairment is named in the notice.

findings.finding: Expectations for New Corteva are low going in: the stock is $11.96 against post-spin targets of UBS $15 (Hold, 2026-10-12), Goldman $20 (Buy, 2026-10-08), JPM $19 (Overweight, 2026-10-06, ~5.7x 2027 EV/EBITDA, near-zero net debt, after a ~$2/share PFAS deduction), and the 20-day run-up is -10.75%; the 2026-11-03 preview reads sentiment as neutral after a 13.1% bullish reading.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The stock rose as much as 9% on JPM's 2026-10-06 upgrade (https://parameter.io/corteva-ctva-surges-after-analyst-sets-19-price-target-post-separation/), so it responds to standalone-value arguments; no earnings reaction for the new perimeter exists.
findings.why_not_priced: This is the price itself, so mostly priced; filed because a first standalone quarter that merely holds the $1.3bn guide meets a bar already lowered by a month of peer damage, and the gap to targets shows the sell side has not cut with the tape.

findings.finding: JPM's 2026-10-06 note puts corn near $5/bu, up ~20% y/y, supporting grower spending on crop protection into 2027, which is the frame for any first 2027 comment on the call.
findings.why_not_priced: A macro input already in a published sell-side note, so mostly priced; it matters only if management uses it to frame a firm 2027 view. Macro-to-company transmission not confirmed by the company, hence small.

findings.finding: Chinese technical (generic active ingredient) prices fell from April to August 2026 and Brazil's Jan-Jul imports ran below 2025 (Agrolink, 2026-10-06): lower raw-material cost for Corteva's margin, and lower generic prices pressuring Brazil pricing; Citi argues Corteva's generic exposure is modest.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 2025 CP EBITDA rose 13% on raw-material deflation and productivity despite price and FX pressure (Q3 2025 release).
findings.why_not_priced: An industry series, partly reflected in the company's own H2 pricing guide; the two effects offset, so it is sized at zero and filed for the judges.

outside_window.finding: Fifteen states and Guam sued in S.D. Indiana (1:26-cv-02122) calling the Vylor spin a fraudulent transfer to escape PFAS liabilities; the district court's 2026-10-09 TRO (no dividends or buybacks, no asset sales outside the ordinary course) was stayed, and a split Seventh Circuit panel granted the stay pending appeal; Corteva told the court it will not declare dividends or buy back stock while the appeal is pending. No ruling or hearing is dated inside the window; a $0.05 dividend is authorised for 2026-12-15 with a 2026-12-01 record date.

baseline_tension: The findings lean negative, against no stated skew (null) but along the -10.75% 20-day run-up, so much of the peer damage is probably already in the price; that is why p_up sits at 44 rather than 35-40.
lessons_applied: Rule 6 (inside what the company guided): the NT 10-Q 'higher seasonal loss' sits inside the guided ~$100m+ Q3 EBITDA loss, so that finding went from -0.3 to -0.1.
Rules 1 and 7 plus the pessimism note (asking what was missed into a print breeds negatives; the run-up already carries the peer damage): p_up moved from 43 to 44, and abs_move was left at 7.0.

'What has worked' (a peer's print landing after the company last spoke leaves consensus stale) and rule 5 (direct counterparties, not macro): the two peer findings stay at -1.0 each and were not shrunk; the corn and generic-price findings stay small as macro proxies.
Rule 6 (verify the bar): the CP-only $1.77bn/$0.09 and the consolidated $2.65bn/-$0.39 reconcile through Vylor's $883m consensus, so no extra cap beyond the moderate sizes already set.
Rule 9 (segment net of the rest): not applicable, because crop protection is now the whole company; seed's Q3 is noise for the price.
